name: PT Star Pacific Tbk

frontmatter.title: Star Pacific — a listed portfolio the market will not pay book for
frontmatter.summary: Star Pacific owns a portfolio of listed Indonesian equities and a small strata-office sub-lease book; it does no development and holds no land bank. Our appraisal of the portfolio, net of a related-party haircut on the common-control holdings and of the cost of running the shell, lands below reported book. Two discounts then compound — the observed holding-company discount and the house marketability limit — and nothing the company has announced closes either. REDUCE.
thesis: The assets are not the question, but they are not free either. The portfolio marks daily, so an appraisal is possible; after a related-party haircut on the common-control holdings and the capitalised cost of the corporate shell, it lands below book, not above it.

Earnings are marks, not operations. The audited FY2025 operating result before the revaluation was a loss, and the nine months to September have already reversed part of the mark that produced the profit.

Two wrapper discounts compound. The discount the shares have held to book is applied to our appraisal, and then the house liquidity limit is applied to the target. Either step alone would put the shares near or above the BUY threshold; together they do not.
Nothing closes the discount. An accumulated deficit blocks any dividend, no buyback is announced, the float is thin and the controlling family has no reason to pay for shares it does not own.
The lease book is shrinking and is almost entirely intra-group rent; the two anchor leases that ended took most of it with them.

catalysts.event: FY2026 audited accounts — the year-end marks on Multipolar Technology and Bank Nationalnobu decide whether the accumulated deficit narrows or deepens
Annual general meeting — any dividend resolution, which the deficit currently blocks
First-quarter accounts — the next quarterly revaluation and the rent run-rate after the two anchor leases ended
Material-fact announcements on the company's investor page — related-party transactions, buybacks

blocks.text: We revise coverage of PT Star Pacific Tbk to a REDUCE rating with a target of Rp154 against a price of Rp188, a total return of -18.2%. Three things changed since initiation. The audited cost base is now in the model: FY2025 operating expenses are IDR26.5bn, not the half-size figure the data pack carried, so the operating business loses more than the pack showed. The RNAV now carries the two deductions an asset appraisal needs — a haircut on the section of the portfolio held inside the group, and the capitalised cost of running the shell — so it is an appraisal rather than reported book by another name. And the P/BV cross-check is held at a lower weight, because its own-history multiple assumes a re-rating we cannot source a catalyst for.

The result is a target below the price. That is not a call on the portfolio: on our appraisal, before the house liquidity step, the twelve-month value is Rp220 a share against today's Rp188, which would be a positive rating on its own. The rating is a statement about two wrapper discounts that compound, and about the absence of anything that would remove either.

The variant view is that Star Pacific is not a property company at all, and should not be valued as one. It reports a single segment, investment and leasing of self-owned or leased real estate, but the leases contribute a fraction of what the balance sheet holds: financial assets total IDR1,750.6bn against a lease book whose investment property is carried at IDR42.4bn [S3]. What the company owns is a portfolio of listed Indonesian equities — Arkora Hydro, Multipolar Technology, Bank Nationalnobu and smaller positions — plus a strata-office sub-lease business that earns rent from related parties [S3]. The profit line is therefore a mark-to-market line, and the operating line is a cost centre.

Three things move the value. First, the marks on the portfolio: FY2025 profit of IDR855.4bn was carried by investment income of IDR830.7bn, and the first nine months of FY2026 have already reversed IDR-293.8bn of it [S2][S3]. Second, whether the accumulated deficit of IDR-549.7bn ever clears, because until it does no dividend is lawful and the shares have no income story [S3]. Third, the discounts themselves, which we treat as structural features of the ownership rather than a mispricing to be arbitraged [S2].

Star Pacific reports one segment: investment and the leasing of self-owned or leased real estate [S3]. The leasing side is a sub-lease business. The company rents space and re-lets it, and the cost of revenue is almost entirely the depreciation of right-of-use assets — IDR5.7bn in the first nine months of FY2026, with no other cost line of consequence [S3]. The property it owns outright is a single investment property carried at IDR42.4bn, immaterial against total assets of IDR1,807.1bn [S3].

The revenue is overwhelmingly related-party. In FY2025, rent from related parties was IDR16.0bn of total revenue of IDR16.6bn, or 96.6% of the total, with third parties contributing IDR0.6bn [S2]. The largest single tenant, PT Matahari Department Store, accounted for 30.0% of FY2025 net revenue [S2]. That concentration matters because both anchors have now gone: the nine-month rent line is IDR7.4bn against IDR12.8bn of operating expense, and the third-party component is the only part of the book that is not an intra-group charge [S3].

The portfolio is the balance sheet. Financial assets total IDR1,750.6bn at the September balance-sheet date. The largest positions are Arkora Hydro at IDR385.3bn held at fair value through profit or loss, Multipolar Technology at IDR361.6bn on the long-term leg plus IDR230.1bn on the short-term leg, and Bank Nationalnobu at IDR310.8bn, the last two at fair value through other comprehensive income, plus other investments of IDR126.0bn and a long-term receivable of IDR101.2bn [S3]. Because the stakes are listed, their value is observable every day; what is not observable is what a buyer would pay for a minority holding in a holding company that owns them, and how much of the book is priced inside the controlling group's own orbit: IDR245.4bn of short-term and IDR674.6bn of long-term investments sit in entities under common control, 13.6% and 37.3% of total assets respectively [S3]. That is more than half of the portfolio, and it is what the discount is made of.

Ownership is concentrated and the group is the Lippo family. PT Inti Anugerah Pratama holds 50.6% and HX Trading Limited 19.5%, together a clear majority, and the company's own disclosures place it inside that group's related-party network [S2]. Strategy, as the annual report states it, is to maintain financial performance and balance-sheet strength rather than to develop anything [S2]. There is no land bank, no marketing sales and no development pipeline: the development slot in our model carries the third-party rent stream, and we say so rather than invent a presales line.

The cost base shows how thin the operating business is. Of the IDR26.5bn of operating expense in FY2025, professional fees and salaries were the two largest items, with custodian and share-administration fees behind them [S2]. Nothing on that list is a development capability: there is no project team, no land acquisition function and no sales force, because there is nothing to build. What the expense buys is the administration of a listed vehicle and the oversight of a portfolio held in small minority positions. That is a legitimate business, but it is an asset-management function run for the benefit of a controlling group, and it is worth what the assets are worth less the cost of running them.

Star Pacific sits between two markets and is a price-taker in both. In Jakarta's strata-office market it sub-lets space to related parties, so its rent is an intra-group transfer rather than a market clearing price; the two anchor leases that ended took most of the related-party rent with them, which is why the nine-month rent line is roughly half the prior full year [S2][S3]. In the equity market it is a minority holder of listed small and mid caps, so the value of its assets is set by other investors' marks, not by anything management does.

Jakarta's office market has carried surplus space since the supply wave that followed the commodity
boom, and landlords in older strata buildings compete on rent and incentives rather than on location
alone. A sub-landlord with a concentrated tenant base has little pricing power once an anchor leaves,
because the space it controls is generic. The listed market that prices Star Pacific's stakes is
similarly outside its control: small-cap Indonesian equities trade on domestic liquidity and foreign
flows, and a holding company's discount is a function of who controls it and what it distributes,
not of the quality of the underlying stakes.

The macro backdrop does not help a rupiah asset with no income distribution. The house deck holds a balance-of-payments-pressure regime with the policy rate at 5.8 rate per cent, CPI at 3.3 rate per cent and real growth at 5.3 rate per cent [S4]. For a company whose earnings are fair-value marks, that combination means the discount rate applied to the marks stays high and the marks themselves stay volatile; there is no rate-driven re-rating to wait for. The property desk's sector stance is AVOID, and nothing in this name argues against it: the operating business has no pricing power and no development pipeline to benefit from a rate cycle.

The second market is where the discount is made. Almost all of the shares sit with the controlling group, so the price is set by the marginal seller in a thin float, and the exchange has already halted the stock once for a sharp move — price discovery in this name is intermittent rather than continuous [S6]. The assets inside the wrapper are liquid and marked daily; the wrapper is not [S3]. That asymmetry, liquid assets inside an illiquid vehicle, is the structural reason the discount exists, and it is also the reason it is not arbitraged away: the arbitrage requires a buyer to finance an illiquid position and then persuade a controller to change its behaviour.

Regulation matters in two places. The accounting treatment of the portfolio — fair value through profit or loss for the trading stakes and through other comprehensive income for the strategic ones — determines whether a mark hits the profit line or bypasses it, and the company uses both [S3]. The listing regime matters more: the exchange suspended the shares in October 2025 for a sharp cumulative price rise and lifted the suspension two weeks later, which is a reminder that a thin float can be halted on the way up as easily as on the way down [S6].

There is no moat. The company cannot set the rent it charges an affiliate, cannot influence the price of its stakes and has no operating capability that a competitor would need to replicate. The one durable competitive feature is the discount itself: it protects an incumbent controller from a takeover and gives a new buyer no way to force a distribution. Five-forces analysis collapses into a single question — who can compel the company to hand back value — and the answer today is nobody [S2][S3].

Revenue has fallen every year in the data we hold: IDR25.0bn in FY2022A, IDR21.0bn in FY2023A, IDR20.6bn in FY2024A and IDR16.6bn in FY2025A, which is a leasing book shrinking as tenants leave rather than a cyclical dip [S2]. The profit line does not follow revenue at all. FY2025 net profit of IDR855.4bn was earned on revenue of IDR16.6bn because investment income contributed IDR830.7bn [S2].

Strip the marks out and the business loses money at the operating level. The audited statement shows gross profit of IDR3.2bn against cost of revenue of IDR13.4bn — cost of revenue being the right-of-use depreciation of the leases and the rent the company pays its landlord — and then operating expenses of IDR26.5bn [S2]. Subtract the second from the first and the all-in operating result is a loss before a single rupiah of investment income. That is the number that matters here, and it is why we treat the FY2025 profit as a mark rather than as earnings. For FY2024 the same comparison gives gross profit of IDR1.5bn on cost of revenue of IDR19.1bn and operating expenses of IDR37.6bn [S2]. The financial summary below carries that audited result rather than the data pack's: FY2025A EBIT of IDR-23.3bn and EBITDA of IDR-23.2bn after 0.02 of fixed-asset depreciation, against the pack's figure, which charged only the half-size cost line. The gap is the point of this section: the pack's operating loss was a third of the audited one, because it booked the 9M25 revenue figure as the cost of revenue [S2 p.134].

The nine months to September show the other side of the same coin. Rent was IDR7.4bn, financial assets at fair value through profit or loss lost IDR-293.8bn, and the period closed with a loss of IDR-264.3bn [S3]. That is not a deterioration in the operating business; it is the mark-to-market engine running in reverse. Equity fell with it, to IDR1,791.5bn, and the accumulated deficit stands at IDR-549.7bn [S3].

The history is the same pattern repeated. FY2024A produced a profit of IDR40.8bn on revenue of IDR20.6bn, again carried by a much smaller investment gain, and other comprehensive income added IDR375.2bn in FY2025 through the revaluation of the strategic stakes [S2]. Equity therefore moves with the marks twice: once through profit and once through other comprehensive income. A reader who follows only the profit line misses half the volatility, and a reader who follows only book value misses that book here is a market price rather than a set of appraisals [S3]. That is why we anchor the valuation on the observed marks and treat the reported equity as a cross-check rather than as the truth.

The balance sheet is simple and unlevered. Total assets are IDR1,807.1bn against total liabilities of a lease obligation; cash is IDR73.1bn and there is no bank debt [S3]. Capital expenditure is de-minimis because the company builds nothing, working capital is immaterial because receivables are intra-group, and there are no financing cash flows at all. Capital allocation is therefore not a decision the company makes: the portfolio is held, the property is held, and nothing is distributed because the deficit forbids it [S3].

Our forecast is mechanical, and it is not a stable top line. FY2026E revenue is IDR8.9bn, -46.3% against FY2025A: the operating business halves, because the full year runs without the two anchor leases that were still paying in the first half of FY2025 and the third-party rent is a fraction of what the related-party rent was [S3]. EBITDA is IDR-13.5bn and net profit IDR-248.8bn, because the operating cost base does not halve with the rent — operating expense stays at 174.0% of revenue, the run-rate the nine-month accounts already show [S3]. From FY2027E rent grows with inflation at the same ratio on costs, which is a constant real cost rather than a margin assumption in our favour. The portfolio is assumed to earn its long-run nominal return from FY2027E rather than to repeat either the FY2025 gain or the nine-month loss [S4].

One modelling caveat we state rather than bury: the forecast balance sheet rolls from the audited FY2025A equity of IDR2,982.5bn, so FY2026E book value overstates the September actual by the fair-value movement already taken through other comprehensive income [S2][S3]. We value the RNAV off the September portfolio marks, not off this forecast line, so the error does not reach the target.

On earnings quality, four flags, and they point the same way. Accruals analysis is meaningless here because the earnings are unrealised marks rather than accruals, but the cash-conversion test fails by construction: no operating cash is generated against a book value that grows on revaluation [S3]. There is no receivables divergence, no capitalised development and no inventory build, because there is no development. Related-party gravity is the dominant flag: 96.6% of FY2025 revenue came from affiliates, more than half the investment portfolio sits in common-control entities [S3], and the group also supplies services to the company, so the operating result is an intra-group allocation rather than a market outcome [S2]. Structure flags are the accumulated deficit and the absence of any distribution mechanism, both disclosed and both binding [S3].

RNAV is the primary method because every large asset on this balance sheet has an observable price. The listed stakes mark daily, the long-term receivable is a contractual claim, and the only judgement is the investment property. An earnings multiple cannot do this job: FY2025 earnings were IDR830.7bn of marks, so a P/E on them capitalises a price that RNAV already contains [S2].

The cost of equity build starts from a ten-year rupiah government yield of 7.4%. We subtract the Indonesian sovereign default spread of 1.6% — the local bond embeds that risk, and the country premium below would otherwise count it twice — and add a levered beta of 0.90 times the sum of a mature-market equity premium of 4.2% and a country risk premium of 2.5%. That gives a cost of equity of 11.9%. Debt is a lease liability priced at 9.4%, the same risk-free plus the house corporate spread, and it carries a negligible weight because the company has no borrowings, so the WACC is 11.9% [S4].

The appraisal is built bottom-up from the September balance sheet, and it is not reported book. The current portfolio of IDR775.5bn is carried at observable marks, less a ten per cent haircut on the IDR245.4bn and IDR674.6bn held in entities under common control: those marks are set in a market where the controlling group sits on both sides, and Multipolar Technology's own long-term mark fell from IDR921.0bn to IDR361.6bn in nine months [S3]. The non-current portfolio of IDR901.8bn enters through the investments bridge, including the IDR101.2bn long-term receivable — a four-year dollar facility to PT Wir Asia Tbk (IDR5.0bn) — which we carry at face because the accounts disclose no impairment against it [S3]. The investment property is capitalised at 5.5% on its FY2026E net rent, which values it below the carrying value of IDR42.4bn: the cap-rate value sits under carrying by that difference, and we state the difference rather than solve the cap rate backwards to reproduce a number. Net debt is net cash, IDR73.1bn against a lease liability. Finally we deduct the cost of the shell: the FY2026E operating expense of IDR15.5bn capitalised at the cost of equity less growth is a permanent claim on the assets that earns nothing, and a static asset value that ignored it would value the portfolio as if the company did not exist. That is a deliberate departure from a gross-asset RNAV, and it is why our appraisal lands below reported book of IDR1,791.5bn rather than at the same number.

Two wrapper discounts then apply, and they compound. We state both, because a reader who sees only the final number cannot tell whether the discount is a view on the assets or on the vehicle. The first is the discount these shares have held to book: 86.0%, set at the most recent year-end level, which takes the appraisal to Rp179 a share and gives the method 85.0% of the weight [S0]. The second is the house marketability limit: with three-month average daily turnover of IDR42.4m the name sits in the lowest turnover band, and the limit applies a 30.0% discount to the target [S0]. Applied in sequence they take the target to Rp154.

That sequence is the rating, and we print it in both directions. Before the liquidity step the twelve-month value is Rp220 against a price of Rp188, which would be a positive rating; with it, the target is Rp154 and the return -18.2%. A reader who believes a fund could own and exit this position should use the first number. Our view is that it could not — a position that cannot be exited is not worth a mark-to-market value — which is why the second number is our target. This is also where a control buyer differs from us: acquiring a majority means settling with holders who have kept the company for years, and the company could distribute the stakes in kind, sell them and pay a special dividend, or buy back shares, but each is lawful only once the deficit is cleared or the board chooses to act, and none is announced [S3].

The table runs the target across the wrapper discount: the columns move nothing because the company has no development revenue, and the rows are the discount itself, from ten points tighter to ten points wider. The row one step tighter already sits above the BUY threshold, which is the honest way to read this name: the rating is a call on a discount, not on the assets.

The P/BV cross-check is the second opinion and it disagrees, as it should. At an own-history multiple of 0.2 on September book of IDR1,791.5bn it gives Rp293 a share, 63.2% above the RNAV method, and it carries 15.0% of the weight [S0]. The gap is not a disagreement about asset value: P/BV asks what the market pays for a rupiah of book and answers with the average of four year-ends, one of which was struck on a book roughly a third smaller than today's; RNAV asks what the assets are worth to this holder and deducts both the related-party and the cost-centre claims explicitly. That is why the multiple is a cross-check at a reduced weight and not a co-equal method — at co-equal weight it would assume a re-rating with no announced catalyst, which is the one thing this company does not offer.

The weighted point value is Rp196. The twelve-month target of Rp220 is that value rolled forward one year at the cost of equity of 11.9%, less the forecast dividend of Rp0, which is nil because the deficit forbids one. We flag the roll rather than bury it: on an asset pool that is marked to market and throws off no cash, compounding at the cost of equity adds to the target without anything in the business having compounded, and it is a horizon convention rather than a source of value. A reader who prefers the as-is number has it above.

What the price implies is instructive. At Rp188 the shares change hands at 0.1x times forecast book, so the market is already pricing a permanent discount and no distribution. To reach our appraisal you have to assume the discount narrows, which requires an event that has not been announced. The price is not obviously wrong; it is a fair price for a company with no mechanism, and the gap between our appraisal and our target is the mechanism itself.

The dominant risk is the portfolio mark, and it is already visible. Arkora Hydro alone carries accumulated unrealised losses of IDR303.8bn [S3]. A repeat of the nine-month mark-down would take another large bite out of book, and because the deficit is already IDR-549.7bn it would push any dividend further away, not closer [S3]. Likelihood high, impact high.

The second risk is that the discount never closes, which is our base case rather than a tail. No dividend is lawful while the deficit stands, no buyback is announced, and the free float is a minority of the shares with a controller that has no incentive to buy it [S2][S3]. Likelihood high, impact medium — it is the difference between our RNAV and the price.

Liquidity is the third. The shares were suspended in October 2025 for a sharp cumulative rise and reopened a fortnight later [S6]. A holder who needs to sell into that market is a price-taker, which is why the target carries the discount it does. Likelihood medium, impact medium.

Governance and related parties are the fourth. Almost all revenue is intra-group and the group also charges the company for services, so the operating result can be moved by decisions taken outside the minority's reach [S2]. Likelihood medium, impact high if a transaction is ever proposed at a price that favours the controller.

Currency risk is not low, and our initiation was wrong to describe the balance sheet as all rupiah. Cash is IDR73.1bn, of which IDR41.9bn is a dollar time deposit and IDR6.7bn a dollar current account, and IDR72.8bn of the total — almost all of it — sits at PT Bank Nationalnobu, an affiliate [S3]. The nine-month result includes an FX gain of IDR26.8bn that flatters it, and the long-term receivable is a dollar facility, so both the profit line and the receivable move with a currency the company does not control [S3]. Regulatory risk is otherwise limited to the listing regime and the suspension precedent [S6].

The portfolio also carries a tax tail we cannot size from the public accounts. Realising the stakes would crystallise gains that are currently unrealised, and the company pays corporate tax on its results, so a sale at today's marks would not deliver the whole fair value to shareholders [S3]. That is an argument for the discount persisting rather than narrowing, and it is one reason we do not treat a sale of stakes as a clean catalyst.

The deficit is not a permanent bar, and the bull case has to say so. It stands at IDR-549.7bn against a portfolio of IDR1,750.6bn [S3], so a mark recovery of under a third clears it, and FY2025 demonstrated exactly that mechanism by adding equity in a year of marks alone [S2]. Once it is cleared, a distribution, a buyback or the sale of the strategic stakes becomes lawful, and even a sale at a blockage discount to the marks would be a multiple of the value the market puts on the shares. That is the bull case and it is a real one; it is not our base case because it requires the controller to choose it.

The bear case assumes the discount widens from where the last three years put it and the portfolio marks down again; the bull case assumes the family releases value once the deficit clears. Both shock the same two drivers in opposite directions, and we weight the base case at 50.0%.

The signposts that would change our view are specific. A distribution, a buyback or a sale of the strategic stakes would compress the discount and move us to a positive rating. A further large mark-down that pushes the deficit beyond any realistic recovery would move us the other way. A related-party transaction at a price below fair value would be a governance event, not a valuation event, and would be treated as such.

Control sits with the Lippo group. PT Inti Anugerah Pratama holds 50.6% and HX Trading Limited 19.5%, leaving a free float of 31.7% [S2]. That structure explains the discount better than any operating fact: a minority holder cannot elect a board, cannot force a distribution and cannot block a related-party transaction.

Related-party dealings are the core governance exposure. Related-party revenue was 96.6% of FY2025 revenue and 84.5% of the nine-month figure, more than half the investment portfolio sits in common-control entities, and the company also pays affiliates for rent, custody and share administration — the rent paid to PT Surya Menara Lestari alone was close to half of cost of revenue [S2][S3]. Every one of those is disclosed, none is hidden, but together they mean the operating result and the marks are both group decisions.

The auditor is KAP Paul Hadiwinata, Hidajat, Arsono, Retno, Palilingan & Rekan, which issued an unqualified opinion on the FY2025 accounts [S2]. The board is chaired by Fendi Santoso as President Commissioner with Surya Tatang as Commissioner and independent commissioners alongside them [S2]. We found no pledge of the controlling stakes disclosed in the shareholder note, and we flag that as absence of disclosure rather than as evidence of no pledge [S2].

The governance machinery is conventional on paper and weak in practice. The annual report describes a board with a president commissioner, a commissioner and independent commissioners, and sets out the general meeting as the venue where shareholders exercise their rights and obtain information [S2]. With a majority holder in place that machinery ratifies more than it constrains: the minority cannot elect a director, cannot set the agenda and cannot outvote the group on any resolution. We therefore treat related-party pricing as a live risk rather than a disclosure formality, and we would want to see the pricing basis for any new intra-group lease or service contract before assuming it is at arm's length [S2].

The dividend record is empty and the reason is structural. The accumulated deficit of IDR-549.7bn means no distribution is lawful until it is cleared, and clearing it requires the portfolio to gain back what the nine-month loss took away [S3]. The shares were suspended on the first of October 2025 for a sharp cumulative price rise and the suspension was lifted on the sixteenth of that month, which is the only listing-regime event on record [S6].

On index treatment, the relevant date has already passed and the answer is nil. From 13 November 2026 the exchange removed from the IHSG calculation the shares it classifies as high-shareholding concentration, under a new test of ten holders or fewer controlling 92.5% or more of the shares, with no market-cap threshold [S7][S8]. LPLI is not among the HSC names confirmed in any source this desk can archive, so no exclusion is booked: two holders account for 50.6% and 19.5% of the shares [S2], and the 383-name list itself is not published in an archived source, so we cannot certify absence — only that the treatment, if it applied, would change nothing here, because three-month average daily turnover of IDR42.4m means passive flow into or out of an index is not a force at this size [S0]. It is not an LQ45, IDX30 or IDX80 constituent either, so the deletions announced for December 2026 do not reach it. We say so because the reverse would matter — passive selling into a float this thin would be the one mechanical force able to widen the discount without any operating news.

On ESG we are thin, and we say so. The company publishes no sustainability report that we could archive, the property exposure is a single strata-office asset, and the portfolio's own ESG profile is whatever its investee companies disclose [S3]. We do not score it, and we do not let the absence of a score stand in for diligence.

The calendar is thin, which is itself the point, but there is one testable catalyst and it is dated. The FY2026 audited accounts in March 2027 publish the year-end marks on the positions that decide everything: Multipolar Technology at IDR361.6bn and IDR230.1bn, and Bank Nationalnobu at IDR310.8bn [S3]. If those marks recover enough to clear the IDR-549.7bn deficit, a dividend becomes lawful for the first time and the discount has a mechanism; if they fall again, the deficit widens and the case for holding the shares weakens. The annual general meeting in the same month is where any dividend resolution would appear [S3]. The first-quarter accounts in April 2027 give the next quarterly revaluation and the first clean read on the post-anchor rent run-rate [S3]. If the deficit is not cleared and no distribution is proposed, we will say plainly that the position is uninvestable at this size rather than keep a rating that depends on a discount nobody has announced a reason to close.

Between those dates we monitor four things. The monthly material-fact page for any related-party transaction, buyback or stake sale [S5]. The quarterly fair-value movement on the Arkora, Multipolar Technology and Nationalnobu stakes, because that single line decides the profit and moves the deficit [S3]. The rent line against the reduced cost base, to see whether the sub-lease business is merely small or actually loss-making [S3]. And the discount itself: if it narrows without a distribution, we will want to know why before we believe it [S2].

bear.narrative: The discount stays where the last three years put it and widens, because nothing forces it shut: no dividend while the deficit stands, no buyback, a 30% free float and a controlling holder with no reason to pay for the rest. In this branch the portfolio also marks down again and book value falls with it.

bull.narrative: The family chooses to release value. The deficit needs only a partial mark recovery to clear, and the last audited year showed exactly that when equity rose on marks alone. Once the deficit clears a dividend is lawful again, and a sale or in-specie distribution of the strategic stakes, even at a blockage discount to the marks, would be a multiple of the market value of the shares. Any of the three compresses the discount toward the tightest level it has held in five years.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs presales growth and RNAV discount

assumptions.label: Presales growth
assumptions.basis: LPLI runs no property development and reports no marketing sales; the September 2026 LK has one segment, investment and leasing of self-owned or leased real estate [S3]. The template's development slot therefore carries the third-party rent stream, not presales, and it is held at the audited annual figure: 557 in FY2025 (F44), grown with 3% inflation, rather than lifted to the quarterly note's 1,146 for 9M26 (F25). The two are not comparable - the same quarterly note shows 1,548 for 9M25 against the annual note's 557 for the whole of FY2025, a difference that has to be a classification (KSO Villa Permata Indah is 23% of quarterly revenue and is treated differently in the two filings), so the annual audited number is the only consistent base. The higher quarterly run-rate is upside we have not assumed, not a figure we can put in the base [S2 p.200 note 19, S3 p.75 note 19].

assumptions.label: Share of presales recognised in the same year
assumptions.basis: Set to 1.0, not the template's 0.5. The slot carries third-party rent, which is billed and recognised in the same period, so there is no presale recognition lag to spread; at the template's 0.5 the model would defer about 0.46 of FY2026E rent into the following year with no sourced reason, which is a default haircut [S2 p.200, S3 p.75].

assumptions.label: Recurring revenue growth
assumptions.basis: Rent from related parties was 16,045 in FY2025 [S2] and 6,227 in 9M26 [S3]: the Matahari Department Store lease (30% of FY2025 revenue) and the Lippo Karawaci lease ended, so FY2026E takes a 48% fall to the exit run-rate and rent then grows with inflation on the house macro path.

assumptions.label: Development gross margin
assumptions.basis: No development revenue exists, so no development margin can apply; the whole gross margin of the company is the leasing margin [S3].

assumptions.label: Recurring gross margin
assumptions.basis: 9M26 cost of revenue is entirely right-of-use depreciation, 5,661 against rent of 7,373, a 23.2% gross margin [S3]; held flat because the lease book and the sub-lease terms are unchanged.

assumptions.label: Cap rate for investment property (RNAV)
assumptions.basis: Set at 5.5% so the capitalised FY2026E net rent gives 36.1 against a carrying value of 42.361 at 30 September 2026 [S3]. The arithmetic is the engine's own: FY2026E recurring revenue of 8.562 x the 23.2% gross margin = 1.986 of net rent, divided by 5.5% = 36.1. The two do not match: the cap-rate value is 6.2 below carrying, and section 4 states that gap rather than solving the cap rate backwards to hide it. The property is one strata-office asset carried at cost and is 2% of RNAV, so the rate is a reconciliation device, not an appraisal.

assumptions.label: Target discount to RNAV
assumptions.basis: The year-end price-to-book has been 0.1695, 0.1697 and 0.1374 in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 (83%, 83% and 86% discounts, datapack S0) and today's price is a further discount to September book. We take the most recent year-end, 86%, one point inside today's level. This is the observed holding-company discount, not a haircut we have chosen: no mechanism narrows it - the accumulated deficit of 549.7 blocks any dividend [S3], no buyback or asset distribution is announced [S5], and the controller has held for years.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 G&A of 26.4 on rent of 16.6 is 159% [S2]; 9M26 G&A of 12.832 on rent of 7.373 is 174% [S3] and is the run-rate we start from. Held flat, not glided: the cost base is salaries (10.4 of the FY2025 26.4), professional fees (10.4) and custodian fees, all of which index to inflation, and rent is grown at the same 3% - so a constant ratio is a constant real cost, not a margin assumption drifting in our favour. A falling ratio would need a cost cut the company has not announced.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Engine default from FY2023A-FY2025A. Note the right-of-use depreciation of 5.7 a year sits inside cost of revenue, not in this line, so EBITDA here is before fixed-asset depreciation only [S3].

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Fixed assets are 1.2 at 30 September 2026 against total assets of 1,807.1 [S3]; the company buys no development land and builds nothing, so capex stays de-minimis at the historical ratio.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Engine default; trade receivables are 236 against related parties and payables nil at 30 September 2026, so working capital is immaterial to the value [S3].

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Engine default of 10%, close to the 19.2/337.4 effective rate of FY2023A and conservative against the 9M26 charge of 767 on a pre-tax loss [S3].

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: The only debt is the PSAK 73 lease liability of 10.0 at 30 September 2026 [S3]. The engine prices debt off the house curve rather than this input: rupiah risk-free 7.45% plus the 200bp corporate spread = 9.45% [S4], and we set the input to the same 9.45% so the input file and the WACC table cannot disagree. Interest expense is immaterial to earnings and to the value.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: Engine default. Deposit yield on the 73.1 cash line [S3]; the interest income of 12.1 in 9M26 is earned on the securities portfolio and is carried in other_nonop instead, so it is not double counted here.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: No borrowing capacity is used: the balance sheet carries 15.6 of total liabilities against 1,791.5 of equity [S3]. The lease liability amortises, but the movement is immaterial, so new borrowing is held at zero.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: The portfolio's expected return. FY2026E carries the reported nine-month loss on financial assets at fair value less the Q4 we do not forecast (-252.0 against -264.3 for 9M [S3]); from FY2027E the portfolio earns 8.6% of its fair value, the house long-run nominal path for Indonesia (real GDP 5.29% plus CPI 3.28%, macro deck). This is an expected return, not a forecast of marks; no alpha is assumed.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Minority interests on the balance sheet are nil at 30 September 2026 [S3].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Zero. The company carries an accumulated deficit of 549.7 at 30 September 2026 [S3], so no dividend is payable under the statutory reserve rule it cites in its own dividend policy [S2]; no dividend has ever been paid in the price history.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Issued and paid-up shares are 1,170,432,803 at 30 September 2026, unchanged since the 2008 rights issue [S3]. The 16,978,418,426 figure some data vendors carry is the authorised capital, not shares outstanding.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: House long-run nominal growth for the rupiah, from the macro deck's long-run anchor, and it sits a point above the 3% we assume for rent growth. It is a DCF input only: no DCF is a method for this company (free cash flow is negative every year and the assets are marked at observable prices), so terminal growth does not enter the value at all.

challenges.challenge: RNAV is 1,776.44 against book of 1,791.54 - 99% the same number - so the '86% target discount to RNAV' is not a discount to an asset appraisal but the observed price-to-book ratio (P/BV 0.1695/0.1697/0.1374 for FY2023-25). Applying the 30% constitution liquidity haircut on top gives 0.75x(NAV x 0.14) + 0.25x(BV x 0.191), rolled at 11.87%, times 0.7 = 182, i.e. 0.098x book and 20% below a market the report calls fairly priced. Nothing in the chain is an independent asset value, and the report never discloses that the two wrapper discounts compound. Dropping either one gives 260, TR +38%, a BUY; the entire HOLD rests on this overlap.
challenges.answer: The RNAV is now an appraisal, not book under another name, and the compounding is printed. Portfolio 775,467 less a 10% related-party haircut on the 920,038 of common-control holdings (F57+F58) less the capitalised cost centre (FY2026E opex 16,310 at 11.85% COE over 3% growth) = 499,199; plus the 901,820 non-current leg, the cap-rate property and net cash the RNAV is 1,500,175, below book of 1,791,540 rather than 99% of it. Section 4 states the 86% holding-company discount and the 30% house liquidity limit as two separate steps, gives the pre-liquidity value of tp_base (a BUY on its own) against the final target, and the sensitivity table runs the target across the wrapper discount. [S3]

challenges.challenge: The report says the stakes are liquid, 'observable every day', and takes no haircut. S3 p.78 note 24 discloses that 920.016 of the 1,750.598 portfolio (52.6%) is held in 'entities under common control' - Multipolar Technology 230.055 current plus 361.600 non-current, Bank Nationalnobu 310.811, Siloam 15.387, Anekatrada 2.185. The same note shows MLPT fair value at 920.975 a year ago versus 361.600 now, a 61% fall, so the marks are neither stable nor independent of the controller. The report also understates the largest holding: it says 'Multipolar Technology at IDR361.6bn' when LPLI holds 591.655bn across the two legs, 33% of RNAV.
challenges.answer: Disclosed and priced. The report now states that 245,442 of short-term and 674,596 of long-term investments sit in entities under common control (13.58% and 37.33% of total assets, F57-F60), that MLPT's long-term mark fell from 920,975 to 361,600 in nine months (F62/F33), and that the MLPT holding is the 230,055 short-term leg (F61) plus the 361,600 long-term leg. The 10% related-party haircut in params.landbank_value applies to that common-control book only, not to Arkora or the third-party investments. [S3 p.78 note 24]

challenges.challenge: Section 3 states 'gross profit of IDR1.7bn against operating expenses of IDR26.4bn'. S2 p.134 shows FY2025 gross profit of 3.201 on revenue 16.602; 1.712 is the 9M26 gross profit (F29), so the sentence splices two periods. Separately, the calibration justification explains the pack by 'charging only 13,240 of cost against gross profit 3,201', but 13,240 is 9M25 revenue in S3 note 19; FY2025 cost of revenue is 13,401 (S2 p.134).
challenges.answer: The period splice is gone. Facts F48-F53 carry the audited FY2025 and FY2024 cost of revenue (13,401 / 19,086), gross profit (3,201 / 1,525) and operating expenses (26,454 / 37,564) from S2 p.134, and section 3 derives the all-in operating loss from gross profit less operating expense for both years. The 9M26 figures stay in the nine-month paragraph. The pack-mapping diagnosis now cites the FY2025 cost of revenue of 13,401, not the 9M25 revenue line. [S2 p.134]

challenges.challenge: The model carries FY2025A EBITDA at -10.02, which the analyst's own qc_justification calls wrong (real all-in -23.253), and the calibration gate is answered with prose rather than a restatement. MOST_LIKELY_BASE_CASE is explicit that wrong data is restated, not modelled around. As a result the QC 'actual' EBITDA margin of -60% against which the -92.4pp drift is measured is itself false (true -140%).
challenges.answer: Cogs and opex facts are in for FY2024-FY2025 and the FY2025A cost base in the model is the audited one (opex 26,454, restated from the pack's 13,240). One limit is stated rather than hidden: the statements print no operating-loss line, so EBIT cannot be restated against a quotable figure and the pack's EBIT survives in that one line. The calibration flag is justified on the audited arithmetic (3,201 less 26,454 = -23,253, a -140% margin) and section 3 names which line is the pack's; we do not use the pack's EBITDA anywhere in the valuation. [S2 p.134]

challenges.challenge: 'FY2026E revenue is IDR9.4bn, a -0.4% fall' - the model's FY2025A 16.602 to FY2026E 9.374 is -43.5%, and the analyst's own recurring_growth is -0.48 and the qc note says revenue falls 44%. A reader of the summary or section 3 is given a stable top line where the operating business in fact halves.
challenges.answer: Corrected. Section 3 now says the operating business halves and prints the model's own revenue growth of fin.FY2026E.revenue_growth against FY2025A, matching the -43.5% line; every other percentage in the section is a model placeholder rather than a typed figure. [S3]

challenges.challenge: The value is rolled forward by 11.87% (method blend 233 to base 260), adding 27.6 per share, or 15% of the final target, on an NAV that is marked at market and whose FY2026E shows a net loss of -249.3 and negative FCFF of -8.3 to -17.5 every year. The disclosed COE build does not produce the rate used: rf 7.45 + 0.902 x (ERP 4.23 + CRP 2.46) = 13.5%, not 11.87%. Section 4 also quotes debt at 9.4% while the input file sets cost_of_debt at 7.5%.
challenges.answer: Reconciled line by line. The engine builds COE as rf 7.45% minus the Indonesian sovereign default spread 1.62% plus beta 0.9022 times (ERP 4.23% + CRP 2.46%) = 11.87%, and section 4 now shows the default-spread subtraction the earlier draft omitted. Debt is the engine's own build, rf 7.45% plus the 200bp corporate spread = 9.45%, and the cost_of_debt input is set to 9.45% so input and table cannot disagree. The roll-forward is disclosed: the point value is v0, the 12-month target is that value compounded at COE less the nil forecast dividend, and we say it is a horizon convention that adds nothing to an asset pool marked at market. [S4]

challenges.challenge: Section 5 asserts 'Currency and regulatory risks are low: the assets and the liabilities are rupiah'. S3 p.55 shows cash of 73.075 of which 59.027 (81%) is on deposit at affiliated PT Bank Nationalnobu, and 41.935 of that is USD; F31 records a 26.805 FX gain in 9M26 that materially flatters the nine-month result. In addition, 101.192 of long-term receivable is carried in the RNAV at face, inside the 'associates/investments' bridge line, with no counterparty or collectability test.
challenges.answer: The all-rupiah claim is withdrawn. Facts F54-F56 show cash of 73,075 with 41,935 in a USD time deposit and 6,695 in a USD current account, 72,845 of it at PT Bank Nationalnobu, an affiliate; F31 records the 26,805 FX gain that flatters the nine-month result. The 101,192 receivable is a USD 5,000,000 four-year facility to PT Wir Asia Tbk (F63), a third party carried at face because the accounts disclose no impairment; section 5 says so and says we have no collectability test beyond that disclosure. [S3 notes 4, 7c and 24]

challenges.challenge: The report treats distribution as structurally impossible ('no mechanism'), yet the deficit is 549.723 against a 1,750.598 portfolio - a 31% mark recovery clears it - and FY2025 demonstrated exactly that: equity rose 1,230.6 in one year on marks. At a 220bn market cap against 1,750.6 of assets, any partial monetisation, even at 50% below marks, is a multiple of the share price. None of this arithmetic appears in the bull case or the signposts.
challenges.answer: The arithmetic is in the report: the deficit of 549,723 against a 1,750,598 portfolio needs a mark recovery of under a third to clear, and FY2025 proved the mechanism by adding equity on marks alone. The bull narrative is rewritten around a distribution once the deficit clears, and a sale or in-specie distribution of the strategic stakes at a blockage discount to the marks; the signposts name the mark recovery as the testable trigger. Probability stays at 25% because it requires the controller to choose it, not because the arithmetic is unfavourable. [S3]

challenges.challenge: The house property card requires a named discount catalyst with a date; the report names the March 2027 audit and AGM only and explicitly says a dividend is unlikely. That leaves a HOLD with no catalyst and a target below the price, and it omits the one testable catalyst the model already carries: the quarterly revaluation of the 591.7 MLPT and 310.8 Nobu positions, either of which can clear or deepen the deficit by itself.
challenges.answer: A dated catalyst is named. The FY2026 audited accounts in March 2027 publish the year-end marks on the 591,655 MLPT position and the 310,811 Nobu position, and those marks decide whether the 549,723 deficit clears; clearing it makes a dividend lawful for the first time. It is in the frontmatter catalysts and section 7, with the AGM in the same month and the Q1 2027 revaluation in April. Section 7 also states plainly that if the deficit is not cleared and no distribution is proposed, the position is uninvestable at this size. [S3]

challenges.challenge: RNAV deducts nothing for the operating cost centre that consumes 16-17bn a year (opex_pct 1.74 on 9.4 of rent; model FCFF is negative every year through FY2035). Capitalised at 11.87% that is ~134bn, 7.5% of RNAV and roughly 6-7% of the final target, and the report never says why a static asset value is the right basis for an entity with a permanent cash burn and no income.
challenges.answer: Deducted. The RNAV now carries the PV of the operating cost centre: FY2026E operating expense of 16,310 at the 11.85% cost of equity over the 3% growth we assume for rent = 184,264, about 12% of the pre-deduction appraisal. Section 4 explains why a static asset value that ignored a permanent cash burn would value the portfolio as if the company did not exist, and params_basis shows the deduction as a named component so the line can be rebuilt. [S3]

challenges.challenge: The P/BV cross-check uses 0.1913x, the mean of four year-end multiples including FY2022's 0.2886, on a series that falls monotonically to 0.1374 (FY2025) and 0.123 today. The method therefore assumes a 55% multiple re-rating with no catalyst, contradicting both the house card ('band mean-reversion, never full-NAV convergence') and section 4's own argument that the discount is structural. On FY2023-25 only (0.1588) the P/BV value is 243, the blend 220 and the target 172, TR -8.5%.
challenges.answer: Part accepted, part rebutted on the mechanism. We cannot change the window: the multiple is the pack's own-history mean of the four year-ends it carries (0.1913) and there is no input to restrict it to three. What we can do is stop it setting the value: P/BV's weight falls from 0.25 to 0.15, section 4 explains that the average includes FY2022's 0.2886 struck on a book roughly a third smaller, states the 63% divergence from the primary openly, and says a co-equal weight would assume a re-rating with no catalyst. The rating is unchanged under the reviewer's own three-year arithmetic. [S0]

challenges.challenge: The model's market block reports mcap_rep of 3,191.9bn because it multiplies the 188 price by 16,978.4m shares - the authorised count the analyst's own share_change basis correctly rejects - against 1,170.4m issued; true market cap is 220.0bn, a 14.5x error. The 83%/83%/86% year-end discount series is also cited to S2/S3, which contain no prices; the figures do check out (P/BV 0.1695, 0.1697, 0.1374 in the datapack, i.e. 83.0%, 83.0%, 86.3%).
challenges.answer: The historical discount series is now cited to S0 rather than to the filings, and the report no longer quotes a market capitalisation, so the 14.5x error never reaches the page. The error is an engine defect, not a file we may edit: cov_engine.market() computes mcap_rep from the pack's balance-sheet share count before applying the restated bs_shares fact, so it prints 3,191.9bn on 16,978.4m shares instead of the 1,170.4m issued. Reported to OPS; multiples and per-share values are unaffected because they use the restated count. [S3 note 17]

challenges.challenge: Section 6 cites [S4] - the internal house macro deck - for 'the exchange's own treatment of concentrated-ownership names has become less forgiving since the start of the year', a BEI regulatory claim S4 cannot support, and section 2 quotes the policy rate at 5.8 against the deck's 5.75. The batch's FTSE Russell (effective 21 Dec 2026) and MSCI Global Small Cap deletions are not tested against LPLI at all.
challenges.answer: The S4 regulatory claim is deleted rather than re-sourced: no dated BEI source for it exists in the archive, so it does not belong in the report. The policy rate is the deck's own 5.75 through the deck placeholder, not a typed 5.8. The index deletions are tested: LPLI is not a constituent at this size and its three-month average daily turnover of 42m rupiah is orders of magnitude below any index liquidity screen, so the FTSE Russell and MSCI removals do not touch it; the test is in section 6 and in valuation.post_bs_review. [S0, S4]

challenges.challenge: Basis errors a reader cannot reconcile: terminal_growth says 4% is 'below the near-term rental growth we assume' while recurring_growth is 3.0%; section 4 and the terminal_growth basis refer to a DCF cross-check the model does not produce (methods are rnav and pbv only, reverse_dcf unavailable, FCFF negative every year); and cap_rate is said to 'reproduce the carrying value' of 42.361 but the model computes 36.117.
challenges.answer: Each statement reconciled. The terminal_growth basis now says 4% sits a point above the 3% rent growth we assume and that no DCF is a method here, so it does not enter the value; the DCF cross-check claims are deleted from section 4; and the cap-rate basis and section 4 now state that the capitalised net rent gives 36.1 against a carrying value of 42.361, a 6.2 gap stated rather than solved away by reverse-engineering the cap rate. [S3]

missing_bull_case.note: Bull rests only on family action. The arithmetic that clears the deficit (549.7 = 31% of a 1,750.6 portfolio; FY2025 equity rose 1,230.6 on marks) is never tested, and no monetisation value is quantified although the portfolio is ~8x the 220bn market cap.

missing_bear_case.note: Absent: 920.0 (52.6%) of the 1,750.6 portfolio is stock of entities under common control with the controller (S3 p.78 note 24), so the 'observable market price' premise is weakest where it matters; MLPT fair value fell 920.975 to 361.600 in nine months; 81% of cash sits at affiliated Bank Nationalnobu including USD 41.9bn.

assumption_realism.note: Opex 174% of rent and the 48% rent fall are sourced and sensible. The 86% discount, the 8.6% portfolio return and the 11.87% COE roll-forward are mutually inconsistent: a portfolio earning 8.6% against a 1% cost drag cannot justify a static discount plus an 11.9% annual value uplift.

evidence_and_citations.note: Verified: financial assets 1.750.598, current portfolio 775.467, deficit 549.723, suspension 1-16 Oct 2025 (S6), related-party revenue 96.6%/84.45%, cash 73.075. Not verified or incorrect: FY2025 gross profit misquoted, FY2026E revenue fall misstated, 30% discount cited to S3, historical discounts cited to S2/S3 not price data, market cap 14.5x too high.

valuation_method_fit.note: RNAV 1,776.44 vs book 1,791.54 (99% identical), so RNAV and P/BV are two multiples on the same book, not independent methods; the 86% target discount is a pricing multiple, and the 30% liquidity haircut compounds it to 0.098x book. No appraisal-based NAV with stake haircuts per the property card, and no PV of the perpetual cost centre.

bias_and_tone.note: The conclusion 'the price is not obviously wrong; it is a fair price' is untestable because the target is built from market-derived discounts; the base case therefore cannot disagree with the price. Prose also says revenue fell 0.4% when it fell 43.5%.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Weights renormalised correctly and the inert development slots are disclosed. But the property card's required named discount catalyst with a date is absent, the policy rate is quoted 5.8 vs deck 5.75, and the batch's FTSE/MSCI deletion news is not checked against LPLI (at a 220bn rupiah cap it is below index size - say so).

conservatism_audit.note: No default haircuts on rent, margin or volume - good. But unjustified optimism is stacked against unjustified caution: the x1.1187 roll-forward of a market-marked NAV, an uncharged ~16bn/yr cost centre, and a P/BV multiple 55% above today's. A 0.098x-book target is not caution, it is a double-count.

calibration.note: The -92.4pp BLOCK is answered with a narrative, not a fix: FY2025A EBITDA is carried at the pack's -10.02 while both report and justification say -23.25. The justification's '13,240 of cost' is 9M25 revenue from S3, not FY2025 COGS of 13,401 (S2). Restate cogs/opex for FY2024-25 and rerun.

signoff.notes: Initiation REDUCE, target Rp154 vs Rp188. Facts and lint PASS; all five BLOCK flags justified on substance from the audited LK arithmetic (opex 26,454 against gross profit 3,201 giving EBIT -23,253), not a re-scoping - restating the data pack 13,240 opex line, which is the 9M25 revenue figure, is correct. Weights renormalised rnav 0.85 / pbv 0.15 properly argued: 830.7 of 847.3 revenue is investment income that RNAV already capitalises at observable prices, so P/E cannot price the name. cap_rate 5.5%, rnav_discount 86% and the rent step-down to the exit run-rate after the Matahari and Lippo Karawaci leases are sourced. NOTE, not blocking: section 4 labels the long-term receivable IDR5.0bn where the fact is USD5.0m; the Rp101.192bn carrying value is correct so only the unit label needs fixing. Length 4,986 words, trim next touch. No konglo flag: the FVOCI portfolio marks Multipolar Technology and Bank Nationalnobu, neither covered here.

bias.note: The round-1 BLOCK is genuinely fixed, not reworded: S2 p.134 audited shows revenue 16.602, cost of revenue 13.401, gross profit 3.201 and operating expenses 26.454, giving EBIT -23.253 and EBITDA -23.235, exactly what the model now carries (F64/F65). The opex restatement reason is now correct and verified: the pack's 13,240 is the 9M25 revenue total in F25, not a cost. The discount stack is not unsourced pessimism - rnav_discount 0.86 is the FY2025 year-end P/BV (0.1374) and today's price/book is 0.1228, so 86% is one point INSIDE the current level, and the report states plainly that pre-liquidity value is Rp220 against Rp188. The 10% common-control haircut is sourced to the 920.0 of the 1,750.6 portfolio held in common-control entities (F57-F60). No unsourced optimism in the other direction: recurring_growth -0.48 follows the Matahari and Lippo Karawaci lease exits (16.045 FY2025 to 7.373 9M26), opex_pct 1.74 is the 9M26 run-rate actually paid, and terminal_growth 4% touches no value because no DCF is a method. Scenarios are mirrored on the same two drivers (presales_growth +/-0.15, rnav_discount +/-0.10) with base 50%.

recomputed.item: 9M25 rent revenue (the line the pack used as opex)

findings.finding: Section 4 calls the long-term receivable a four-year 'IDR5.0bn' dollar facility; F63 shows USD5.0m. The appraisal uses the reported IDR101.192bn carrying value, so the value is right and only the unit label is wrong.
Report is 4,986 words against the 500-3,500 update band. No number is affected.

flags.message: FY+1 ebitda margin moves -11.8pp from FY2025A: source the change
flags.justification: FY2025A is the audited base, not the pack's: revenue 16,602 (F3), cost of revenue 13,401 (F48) and operating expenses 26,454 (F52) give EBIT of -23,253 (F64) and, after 18 of fixed-asset depreciation, an EBITDA of -23,235 on a -139.9% margin [S2 p.134]. FY2026E's -151.7% is that same cost base held at 1.74x rent while rent falls 44% to the 9.4 run-rate after the Matahari and Lippo Karawaci leases ended [S3 p.75 note 19]. The 11.8pp gap is the revenue fall against a cost base that does not fall with it, not a margin assumption.

flags.message: opex FY2025A restated at 2.00x the data pack: say why the pack is wrong
flags.justification: The data pack carries FY2025 operating expenses of 13,240 against an audited 26,454 (F52); 13,240 is the nine-month 2025 revenue line in S3 note 19, not a cost, and the pack has picked it up in place of the expense. The audited statement charges 26,454 of operating expense below gross profit of 3,201 [S2 p.134], which takes FY2025A EBIT from -10,039 to -23,253. The pack's figure would show a company with half the cost base it actually has.

flags.message: ebit FY2025A restated at 2.32x the data pack: say why the pack is wrong
flags.justification: The pack's FY2025 EBIT of -10,039 reconciles only if operating expenses are the pack's 13,240. The audited statement charges 26,454 (F52) against gross profit of 3,201 (F50), so EBIT is -23,253 (F64) and EBITDA -23,235, a 2.32x restatement. EBIT is a restatable line and this is the filing's own arithmetic, not a re-scoping; the pack has mapped the 9M25 revenue figure into the cost line [S2 p.134].

flags.message: balance-sheet cash restated at 0.09x the data pack: say why the pack is wrong
flags.justification: The pack's 844,552 of cash adds two lines the filing keeps apart: cash and cash equivalents of 73,075 and other current financial assets at fair value of 775,467 [S3 p.4 and note 6]. We restate cash to the 73,075 actually on deposit and carry the 775,467 securities portfolio in the RNAV land-bank slot, with the 901,820 non-current leg through the investments bridge, so the portfolio is counted once at its observable fair value instead of twice [S3 note 7].

flags.message: balance-sheet investments restated at 644.16x the data pack: say why the pack is wrong
flags.justification: The pack carries 1.4 of investments, which is only the associate line; the LK's non-current financial assets total 901,820 at 30 September 2026 - FVOCI stakes in Multipolar Technology 361,600 and Bank Nationalnobu 310,811, other investments 125,986 and a 101,192 long-term receivable [S3 p.60 note 7]. That is half of book equity and the largest single driver of RNAV, so the 644x restatement is the pack missing the portfolio, not us revaluing it [S3 p.4].
